articles.title: Here are the 30,000 songs Sony is suing Udio’s AI music generator over
articles.summary: Sony is suing the AI music-making tool Udio, claiming the company infringed on more than 30,000 of its songs.
articles.body: Sony Music Entertainment has filed another lawsuit against Udio, accusing the AI music generator of infringing the copyright of more than 30,000 of its songs, ranging from Elvis Presley’s Hound Dog to Beyoncé’s Say My Name, and Harry Styles’ As It Was. The lawsuit, filed in a New York court on Monday, claims that this list represents “only a small portion of Plaintiffs’ works that Udio infringed,” as reported earlier by Music Business Worldwide. In 2024, Sony, along with Universal Music Group and Warner Records, filed a lawsuit against Udio and the AI music-maker Suno. After gaining access to Udio’s training data through discovery, Sony claims it identified additional songs using an “audio fingerprinting” technique. Sony filed a request to add more than 30,000 songs that Udio allegedly “copied and ingested into its generative AI models,” but a judge later rejected the company’s motion, leaving the scope of the original lawsuit at 333 works. Sony has now made the more than 30,000 songs the subject of its new lawsuit, which the company says it could expand. It claims Udio “admitted that its generative AI models were ‘constructed by showing the program a vast amount of different kinds of sound recordings,’” including from YouTube. UMG and Warner Music Group have since settled with Udio and are now partnering with the company as the music industry embraces AI. You can read the full list of songs Sony is suing Udio over in this filing. The company is asking to block Udio from infringing its works, as well as for up to $150,000 per work infringed.

articles.title: West of England in pictures: Forwards Festival and Blood Moon
articles.summary: Festivals, tributes and awards in photographs from across the West this week.
articles.body:
This week in the West, music lovers danced in the rain at Forwards Festival and stargazers marvelled at the magical Blood Moon during the partial lunar eclipse.

Some stunning aerial shots also showed how parched the landscape remains despite the showers.

Here is our round-up of photographs from across the West this week.

Dancing in the rain: Music lovers bid farewell to summer at Forwards Festival in Bristol.

For the first time in the music event's history, every stage was powered by renewable energy .

Royals: About 23,000 people turned up to watch Forwards Presents: Lorde on the Clifton Downs on Friday. The main festival concludes on Sunday.

Cup clash: Bristol Rovers took on Chelsea's youngsters – now known as Cobham Next Gen - in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday night. The match finished 2-2 but the London club won the following penalty shoot-out.

Blood moon: A partial lunar eclipse gave the moon an eerie reddish glow on Friday. BBC Weather Watcher Lybby captured this photograph from Yatton.

Celebrating independence: Monday was Ukraine's 35th independence day, marking the date the country formally broke away from the Soviet Union on 24 August 1991. At City Hall in Bristol, there was an event featuring traditional dancers and Ukrainian food.

To the seaside: North Somerset Council is trialing specialist wheelchair-accessible beach matting at Weston-super-Mare to help people with disabilities navigate the sand.

Africa to the Cotswolds: This Hummingbird hawk-moth was spotted in Gloucestershire. The day-flying species migrates from North Africa and Southern Europe each summer. Recent summer heatwaves and southerly winds have driven an increased influx in the county.

Parched land: These pictures taken from a flight over Gloucestershire and an aerial view over Cheltenham Racecourse show how the summer has left the landscape looking parched and dry.

After the rain: Stormy skies gathered over Gloucestershire Cathedral this week following a downpour, as much-needed rain arrived after a long period of dry weather.

Get moving: The Age UK Gloucestershire team took part in a dance fitness session as part of a new campaign which encourages people in mid life to embrace movement.

Winged flight: Thank you to BBC Weather Watcher CraigRich, who caught this photo of a Hummingbird Hawk Moth as it landed on a flower in Winterslow

Chippenham will always love you: Humphrey & Co accountancy in Chippenham have paid tribute to superstar Dolly Parton with a life-size cut out of the singer on display this week.

Team effort: Volunteers from British Gas rolled up their sleeves this week to help clear several skip loads of waste from inside Swindon's former tented market building in the town centre.

Oyez, oyez: Charlotte Howard, a horticulturist and actor, has been crowned the new Town Crier of Devizes , and is the first woman to hold the title.

Messages in the sand: Campaign group 38 Degrees organised a large message on the beach at Burnham-on-Sea calling on the Prime Minister to return water companies back to public ownership in a bid to reduce sewage discharges.

The Environment Agency said: "We know Burnham-on-Sea is a popular destination and that's why we are working closely with Wessex Water to improve the water quality within the wider catchment.

"We are regulating trials of natural ways to treat storm overflows discharges to help protect water quality."

Nation's favourite: The Strawberry Line path which runs through Somerset was named Britain's favourite path by walking charity The Ramblers following a month-long public vote.

Staff Praise: Patients praised teams at the Royal United Hospitals Bath (RUH) NHS Foundation Trust for treating them with kindness and compassion in the results of a newly published survey.

articles.title: Melania Trump Suggests Son Barron, 20, Is ‘Happy’ They Don’t See Each Other Often
articles.summary: Melania Trump gave some insight into her relationship with son Barron, hinting that he might be okay with the fact they don’t all get together as a family as...
articles.body:
Melania Trump hinted that her son Barron might be okay with their family not getting together as much as they used to.

Melania praised the importance of making a schedule to balance her busy life with her husband's presidential duties and Barron's studies at New York University.

Barron Trump has reportedly become more cautious and reclusive following the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk in September 2025.

Melania Trump gave some insight into her relationship with son Barron , hinting that he might be okay with the fact they don't all get together as a family as much as they used to.

The first lady, 56, appeared as a guest on Fox Business's The Big Money Show on Wednesday, September 23 and was asked by cohost Taylor Riggs about juggling her personal and professional life. During the chat, she appeared to suggest her 20-year-old son is okay with having a little distance between them.

"You are so busy and you're such an inspiration to young moms out there who are trying to do it all — run businesses, charities, organize state dinners, run a family. Do you still try to get your family together for Sunday night dinners or try to see Barron when you can?" Riggs wondered.

Riggs then asked, "What are pieces of advice for moms who feel like they're so stretched thin, trying to do it all, but at the end of the day just want maybe a dinner at night with their family?"

First, Melania praised the art of making a schedule, especially "because everybody's so busy." Her husband President Donald Trump , of course, is preoccupied with his presidential duties, while Barron is currently attending New York University.

"My husband is working, sometimes he's in the Oval Office until 9:30 at night, so do you wait that you will have dinner? You don't," the former model said. "Because he's busy, I'm busy too. But we try to find time."

Melania continued, "It's less and less, the family time is suffering because of it. But that's okay. We are here to work, to do a good job, and that's what matters."

Of her son, she added, "Barron is already a young man, so sometimes he's maybe even happy that I just want to do my stuff. And that's okay."

Her comments come after a report from the New York Post published on August 28, described Barron as "pretty reclusive" as ongoing threats against his family have largely kept him out of the public eye.

"He doesn't go out," another source told the publication.

The president's youngest son reportedly became even more cautious following the September 2025 assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk , whom the Post said Barron had grown close to .

"This is what happens when you go out there," he reportedly told his father when he learned of Kirk's death.

The comment was first reported by Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan in their book, Regime Change , according to the outlet.

articles.title: Are you Team Manuscript or Team Letter? The twists in 'Verity,' explained.
articles.summary: The new film starring Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson has a famously ambiguous ending.
articles.body:
The real twist in Verity is entirely dependent on what you see as the truth.

The latest Colleen Hoover adaptation starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett is a psychological thriller with a wild twist, one that has stirred fan debate since the book's 2018 publication. With director Michael Showalter's film sticking closely to the novel's original rug pull, theatergoers who haven't read the novel can finally choose whether they're "Team Manuscript" or "Team Letter," and fight with their friends about it on the way home.

No idea what that means, or just want a refresher? Warning: Only darkness (and major spoilers for the twist in Verity ) ahead.

Verity stars Johnson as Lowen Ashleigh, a struggling writer who gets the opportunity of a lifetime when she's asked to ghostwrite the final books in author Verity Crawford's (Hathaway) series of thrillers. Verity can't finish the novels, which are all told from the perspective of the villain, because she was injured in a serious car accident — one that her husband Jeremy (Hartnett) has been careful to keep out of the press.

Lowen agrees to write the novels, as she needs the money after her late mother left her in debt. And because this is a psychological thriller, she also agrees to live in Verity's beautiful-but-isolated home in Vermont, with Jeremy and Verity's young son Crew (Brady Wagner), in order to have easy access to Verity's disorganized notes. When Lowen gets to the house, however, she is surprised to find that Verity's condition is worse than she was initially told: the author isn't just injured, but paralyzed — she's unable to walk, speak or move.

So, Lowen dives into Verity's files in hopes of being able to write in Verity's voice. What she discovers, however, is something far darker than she could have imagined. Hidden in Verity's cigarette box is a USB drive containing a secret manuscript the author wrote, which she claims is her raw, honest autobiography. And that's where the twist begins…

Lowen begins reading. At first, she's intrigued by Verity's titillating details of her romance with the charming and kind Jeremy. Then, however, she's disturbed by how Verity appears to have a sharp disdain for her son Crew and her daughter Harper (Sienna Kulovitz), who died in a canoe accident less than a year earlier.

But the longer Lowen lives in Verity's shadow, the more she suspects that Verity isn't actually incapacitated. Lowen is sure she sees Verity moving around the house, something that Jeremy assures her is impossible. And it's easy enough for Lowen to write this off as a manifestation of her own guilt, especially as she grows closer to — and eventually falls for — Jeremy, who seems like a doting father and loyal husband.

Everything changes, however, when Lowen gets to the end of Verity's manuscript. The autobiography details how Verity not only hated her children and resented them for stealing Jeremy's affections — she also wanted them dead. Verity, according to her own autobiography, planned the canoe trip in order to orchestrate Harper's drowning, hoping that with one less kid around, Jeremy would pay more attention to her.

Alas, Verity is disappointed to find that this master plan didn't work at all; Jeremy's too grief-stricken to show Verity affection. The autobiography ends with a disappointed Verity declaring that she plans to drive herself into a tree if Jeremy doesn't come around, which is exactly the accident that led to Verity's current physical state.

How Verity turns the tables on us yet again

Lowen is shocked and horrified. But it also gives credence to Lowen's theory that Verity is an evil, manipulative monster who is faking being incapacitated. Lowen just can't get Verity to break on her own.

So, Lowen shows Jeremy the manuscript, insisting it's proof that Verity has recovered from her car accident and is secretly capable of moving and speaking. Jeremy reads what Verity wrote and confronts his wife in her bedroom. In a shocking moment, Verity springs to action, insisting she can "explain everything" to Jeremy.

It falls on deaf ears, though. Jeremy strangles Verity, attempting to kill her — until Lowen intervenes. She tells Jeremy not to strangle Verity, as he'll get caught for her murder, and Crew wouldn't have a father to care for him. But Lowen's not being kind, just practical: She instructs Jeremy to smother Verity instead, so as not to leave a mark. He does so, and the two take Verity's body to the lake and throw it in, later lying to the police about Verity exiting the house on her own.

But wait — the twist in 'Verity' also has a twist!

After Verity's death, the film flashes forward seven months. Lowen is pregnant with Jeremy's baby and the couple is moving with Crew to North Carolina, out of the home Jeremy once shared with Verity. Lowen follows Crew into his room to get the last of his things, when she sees a floorboard popping up, revealing Crew's secret hiding place. Beneath the floorboard, Lowen finds a letter from Verity… and it changes everything.

The letter is addressed to Jeremy. Verity says that if Jeremy is reading this, she and Crew are somewhere safe. She explains how the manuscript for her autobiography — in which she claimed to hate her kids and plotted Harper's death — was an exercise introduced to her by her editor after Harper died in the canoe accident. The letter reframes Verity's manuscript not as an admission of truth, but as an example of "antagonistic journaling," in which Verity deliberately expressed the exact opposite of her real feelings.

But Verity writes that Jeremy found the manuscript and read it (even though Jeremy only read one of her previous novels.) According to the letter, Jeremy was so enraged that Verity killed Harper that he drugged her and orchestrated her car accident as punishment. Realizing Jeremy was a danger to her, Verity faked being permanently paralyzed as a way to keep herself safe until she could get herself and Crew away from Jeremy. She was sure that if Jeremy thought she was healthy again, he would turn her in to the police for killing Harper (which she insists she didn't do) or he'd attempt to murder her a second time.

The letter gives Lowen, not to mention the audience, quite a lot to consider. Was Verity telling the truth in her manuscript or in her letter? Ultimately, Lowen decides she'll never be able to know. Verity was a master at manipulating the truth, after all… it's just unclear what truth she was manipulating.

The original version of the Verity novel leaves the situation entirely ambiguous, much like the film. But in 2022, Hoover released a bonus chapter that seemed to tilt things in the favor of Team Letter — that Jeremy really did try to kill Verity, and that her letter was the truth.

This bonus chapter shows Jeremy and Lowen in their new life in North Carolina, where they've disappeared to after the tragedies in Vermont. But in their new life, a woman from Vermont recognizes Jeremy and Lowen. Jeremy freaks out and drowns her as Lowen watches it unfold. So, while it's not a definitive answer as to whether Jeremy's capable of very dark things, it's certainly a suggestion that he could have tried to kill Verity after reading her manuscript.

Of course, all of this really means nothing: Many different versions of the story are technically possible. Perhaps Jeremy did try to kill Verity, but her manuscript is also the truth. Or maybe Verity planted that letter as collateral in case Jeremy tried to kill her again, as a plot to mess with Lowen for stealing her life.

As for Hoover, she hasn't declared which twist is the real twist… meaning that it's all really up for interpretation.

articles.title: Bruce Willis' wife makes emotional promise as actor enters 'next chapter'
articles.summary: Emma Heming Willis honored husband Bruce Willis during World FTD Awareness Week, calling him the driving force behind her advocacy.
articles.body:
Bruce Willis ' wife, Emma Heming Willis , is honoring the actor's legacy while advocating for families facing frontotemporal dementia.

In an Oct. 1 Instagram post marking World FTD Awareness Week, Heming Willis dedicated a message to her husband, explaining how his illness has shaped her efforts to raise awareness.

"I can't go through World FTD Awareness Week without talking about Bruce. He is the driving force behind my advocacy," she wrote.

Heming Willis said the "Die Hard" star has created opportunities for her to speak out, and she intends to keep using them to support others.

"I will not let his diagnosis be in vain," she added. "I know how proud he would be to know that he is helping families living with FTD, other forms of dementia and their care partners be seen and heard."

Heming Willis also reflected on his enduring legacy, describing this stage of his life as another chapter in it and expressing pride in being his wife.

When was Bruce Willis diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia?

Willis, 71, stepped away from acting in March 2022 after his family announced he had aphasia, a condition that affects communication. In February 2023, they publicly shared a more specific diagnosis: frontotemporal dementia.

FTD encompasses a group of brain diseases affecting the frontal and temporal lobes, which help regulate personality, behavior and language, according to the Mayo Clinic . Symptoms vary and generally worsen over time.

Emma Heming Willis speaks out about caregiving and grief

The tribute follows Heming Willis' September comments about her family's ongoing grief as they adapt to changes caused by the progressive illness.

Speaking to HELLO! magazine , she described the emotional difficulty of those changes while emphasizing that their lives still include laughter, affection and connection.

"It is extremely difficult and painful," Heming Willis said. "It's natural, we all want our loved ones to be healthy, full of life and being the person they always were. But FTD is a devastating illness that steals things from you very slowly. So the reality is that you find yourself constantly in a state of grief."

'Moonlighting' to McClane: The roles that made Bruce Willis a legend

In 1991, Willis played a private eye investigating a murder alongside a disgraced ex-football star (Damon Wayans, left) in "The Last Boy Scout." The film's director, Tony Scott, found success with movies such as "Beverly Hills Cop" and "Days of Thunder."

The couple married in 2009 and share daughters Mabel, 14, and Evelyn, 12. Willis also shares daughters Rumer , 38, Scout , 35, and Tallulah , 32, with ex-wife Demi Moore.

His family continues to share moments together publicly. Earlier this week, Tallulah posted a photo of herself kissing her father's forehead after he attended her wedding to musician Justin Acee in August.

articles.title: Claudette Soares lança em novembro álbum batizado com música feita para a cantora por Zélia Duncan e Ana Costa | G1
articles.standfirst: O repertório do álbum 'O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar' inclui parcerias inéditas de Marcos Valle com Tim Bernardes, de Roberto Menescal com Joaquim e de Zé Manoel com Ronaldo Bastos.
articles.summary: O repertório do álbum 'O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar' inclui parcerias inéditas de Marcos Valle com Tim Bernardes, de Roberto Menescal com Joaquim e de Zé Manoel com Ronaldo Bastos.
articles.body:
Claudette Soares canta músicas de Zé Manoel, Tim Bernardes, Marcos Valle, Joaquim e Roberto Menescal no álbum 'O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar' — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Um dos bordões de Claudette Soares, “O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar” não somente virou música, como deu nome à composição que batiza o álbum que a cantora lançará em novembro, quando já estiver com 91 anos.

“O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar” é música inédita composta por Ana Costa e Zélia Duncan especialmente para a cantora carioca, nascida em 31 de outubro de 1935.

Arquitetado por Marcus Preto em 2023, o álbum foi formatado com repertório inteiramente inédito – todo composto especialmente para Claudette – e com produção musical do próprio Marcus Preto com Thiago Big Rabello.

Além da música-título “O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar” (Ana Costa e Zélia Duncan), o repertório do álbum é composto por músicas como “Batuque bom” (Marcos Valle e Tim Bernardes), “Bem feliz” (Zé Manoel e Ronaldo Bastos), “Esse escurinho é você” (Roberto Menescal e Joaquim), “Natural” (Zé Renato e Nando Reis) e “Viva” (Marcos Valle e Arnaldo Antunes), além da já conhecida “O prazer de viver para mim é você” (2024).

“O prazer de viver para mim é você” é (grande) música de Guilherme Arantes, gravada por Claudette com o próprio Arantes e lançada em single há dois anos, precisamente em maio de 2024, ainda durante o processo de gravação do álbum.

articles.title: 'The Family Man' actress Gul Panag renews pilot licence after 10 years; ‘Allowing myself a small pat on the back’
articles.summary: Along with being a celebrated actress, Gul Panag is also a licensed private pilot.
articles.body: Along with being a celebrated actress, Gul Panag is also a licensed private pilot. The 'Dor' actress got a little nostalgic as she recently renewed her licence after 10 years.Looking back at the time when she first got her licence, Gul Panag wrote on her IG, "Life is eventually all about perspective. Ten years ago, when I got my flying licence, I was over the moon. It had been on my bucket list for a very, very long time. And there had been no shortage of people telling me I couldn't do it. Or wouldn't be able to (sic)."The 'The Family Man' actress also reflected on all the hurdles she had to overcome to realize her dream of becoming a pilot."Starting flying training is one thing. Completing the prescribed flying hours while pursuing a career, clearing all the exams, navigating the paperwork, keeping your medical current and seeing the entire process through is quite another. Individually, they're all relatively simple things. Together, they add up to a great deal, especially when you're not doing it to pursue flying as a profession. But I managed. And when that licence was finally issued, I was ecstatic. A huge bucket-list item ticked off," she penned.Gul Panag said that ten years after officially becoming a pilot, she realised that getting the licence was one thing; keeping it is quite another.She added that she knows so many people who started flying but never finished their training, or others who completed their flying hours but do not clear the exams. And then there are those who earned their licences but eventually let them lapse."Life, work, medical requirements, or simply not flying enough. It happens so easily, particularly when flying isn't your profession," she added."I now appreciate not just what it took to get here, but what it has taken to keep going. And for once, I'm allowing myself a small pat on the back. Walking in this time, not as a student hoping to earn her wings, but as a licensed pilot returning for a renewal, felt rather different. articles.title: Box Office: ‘Digger’ Majorly Bombs With $8 Million Opening Weekend, ‘Verity’ Scores $32 Million Debut
articles.summary: In “Digger,” Tom Cruise portrays a powerful oil tycoon who is bracing for an ecological disaster of epic proportions. But nothing could have prepared him for...
articles.body:
In "Digger," Tom Cruise portrays a powerful oil tycoon who is bracing for an ecological disaster of epic proportions. But nothing could have prepared him for the catastrophe that's unfolding at the box office, where "Digger" has collapsed with an embarrassing $8 million from 3,321 North American theaters. Rivals believe the figure will be closer to $7.5 million when the final numbers are tallied on Monday.

With a production budget of $160 to $180 million, "Digger" will wind up as not just one of the biggest bombs of the year but potentially of all time. Warner Bros. was hoping the combination of Tom Cruise, one of the biggest movie stars in the world, and director Alejandro González Iñárritu, whose critical and commercial wins include "Birdman" and "The Revenant," would at least propel initial grosses to $18 million to $20 million. And even those ticket sales would have been financially disastrous for the mega-budgeted satirical film. Box office experts say a movie of this size would have needed a debut near $40 million to justify its price tag. Those projections were revised down (and revised down again) after a deluge of bad buzz. The R-rated satire opened in fifth place behind another newcomer, Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson's psychological thriller "Verity," and three holdovers, including "Resident Evil" and "Heart of the Beast."

"For a black comedy, the numbers are not bad. But black comedies are small films, and this isn't a small film. It's a Tom Cruise movie," says analyst David A. Gross of Franchise Re. "The comedy walks a fine line, and when it misses, it misses ."

Reviews and word-of-mouth for "Digger" have been so negative that Warner Bros. tried to embrace the unfavorable press . In a recent ad, the studio told moviegoers to "decide for yourself" after critics bashed the movie as "unpleasant" and "baffling." Another marketing spot suggested that only American audiences disliked "Digger." However the movie was equally rejected at the international box office with a tragic $12 million from 73 international markets for a global start of $20 million.

"Digger" was always a gamble as the rare big-budget, star-driven R-rated original comedy. Warner Bros. greenlit the film for $125 million, but the price tag soared after production ran long. Since the studio spent another $100 million on global marketing efforts, "Digger" has a theatrical break-even point of roughly $350 million globally, according to executives with knowledge of similar films. A Warner Bros. spokesperson pushed back, saying the film's break-even point is $300 million. Either way, "Digger" is primed to lose at least $150 million to $200 million theatrically. (Theater owners keep roughly half of ticket sales.) Profitability for the studio will take even longer because Cruise gets first-dollar gross, meaning he earns a percentage of revenues before the studio recoups any costs.

"Even with respectable ancillary income based on the film's pedigree," says Gross, referring to revenue streams like digital rental, sales, streaming and TV licensing, "the movie is going to lose a lot of money."

"Digger" extends a dismal year for Warner Bros. — having fielded such misfires as "The Bride" and "Supergirl" — and the timing was terrible. Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. is set to close next week . News broke on Friday that Warner co-chief's Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy are leaving the studio when the merger closes on Oct. 6. The duo enjoyed a terrific box office run in 2025, with a stellar string of hits including "Sinners," "A Minecraft Movie" and "Weapons." But after pushing a number of big swings into 2026, not a single film has managed to cross $100 million domestically.

This time last year, few in Hollywood would have expected "Verity" to prevail over "Digger" at the domestic box office. Amazon MGM's adaptation of Colleen Hoover's best-seller has landed in first place with a solid $32.6 million from 3,510 theaters. It ranks as Hathaway's third No. 1 opening of 2026 after this summer's blockbusters "The Devil Wears Prada 2″ and "The Odyssey." A very pregnant Hathaway has recently joked that she's now going to disappear for the rest of the year .

"Verity" collected another $30 million at the international box office, bringing its worldwide tally to $62.5 million.

Directed by "The Big Sick" filmmaker Michael Showalter, "Verity" centers around famed author Verity Crawford (Hathaway) who gets badly injured in a car accident, leaving her husband (Josh Hartnett) to hire a struggling writer (Johnson) to complete the remaining books in the popular series. Reviews and word-of-mouth has been negative; the film was saddled with a "C+" grade on CinemaScore and 34% on Rotten Tomatoes. However, "Verity" was produced for $40 million and is expected to turn a profit for Amazon MGM.

"This is an excellent opening," Gross says. "The reception is not hurting the film. Audiences are showing up in big numbers."

Hollywood has been eager to mine Hoover's novels for the big screen because her work caters to an underserved female demographic, and the film adaptations carry modest production budgets, making them low-risk bets for studios. Opening weekend crowds for "Verity" were 78% female, while the largest age demo (38%) were between 25 and 34 years old. Among Hoover's adaptations, "Verity" registers the second-biggest debut behind Sony's 2024 sleeper hit "It Ends With Us" ($50 million) and ahead of Paramount's 2025 film "Regretting You" (13.6 million) and Universal's 2026 movie "Reminders of Him" ($17 million). "It Ends With Us" is the highest-grossing of the trio by far with $350 million globally.

With general audiences rejecting "Digger," Sony's video game reboot "Resident Evil" remained in second place with $12.5 million in its third weekend of release. So far the R-rated movie, directed by "Weapons" filmmaker" Zach Cregger, has generated a strong $124.8 million domestically and $215 million globally against a $75 million budget.

"Resident Evil" is the second consecutive box office win for Sony following "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," which has now generated a staggering $954 million in North America and $2.5 billion globally. It's the third-highest grossing movie in history behind "Avengers: Endgame" ($2.925 billion) and "Avatar" ($2.923 billion). Thanks to Disney's recent re-release of "Avengers: Endgame," which has collected a huge $126 million in two weekends, the Marvel behemoth once again ranks as the biggest release of all time . Disney reissued the blockbuster (with extra footage) to generate hype for "Avengers: Doomsday," which lands on the big screen in December.

Third place went to "Heart of the Beast" with $11 million in its sophomore outing, a 45% decline from its debut. So far, the Brad Pitt-led survival thriller has grossed $38.3 million in North America and $98.6 million worldwide and will imminently cross the $100 million mark. Since Paramount spent $82 million to produce the well-reviewed film, "Heart of the Beast" will rely on staying power and interest at the international box office to recoup in its theatrical run.

"Primetime," a psychological drama starring Robert Pattinson as "To Catch a Predator" host Chris Hansen, landed at No. 4 with $8 million in its second weekend. That's a steeper 58% drop from its strong $19 million opening. So far, "Primetime" has amassed $34 million in North America against a modest $15 million budget. The movie, backed by A24, has yet to open in most international territories.

Through this weekend, the domestic box office stands at $7.95 billion, up 19% from the same point in 2025, according to Rentrak. Now the market is roughly $50 million away from crossing $8 billion — a milestone the industry didn't cross last year until December.

"September certainly did its part," says Rentrak's head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian, referring to releases like "Resident Evil" and "Primetime." "For a month that has often been viewed as something of a transitional period on the theatrical calendar, that is another strong indication of the depth and durability of the 2026 marketplace."

articles.title: In 2022, Ben Affleck founded an AI company; the actor, who once saw artificial intelligence as a threat, sold his firm to an OTT giant in 2025 and has now used its technology in his latest film, ‘Animals’
articles.summary: Discover how Ben Affleck transitioned from fearing AI in filmmaking to successfully integrating it in his latest film 'Animals', and the implications for the future of Hollywood.
articles.body: Ben Affleck once saw artificial intelligence and thought Hollywood might be in serious trouble. Now, the actor-director has used AI in his own movie. Affleck revealed this week that artificial intelligence was used “for lots of things” in ‘Animals’, his new thriller. The surprising part is not simply that he used AI. It is what happened before this.He went from worrying about what AI could do to filmmaking to building a company around it, selling that company to Netflix and now using the technology in one of his own films.But Affleck insists there is a line between using AI to help make a movie and letting AI make the movie.Ben Affleck used AI in ‘Animals,’ but won't reveal where Speaking at Bloomberg’s Screentime event on October 1, 2026, Ben Affleck was asked about AI’s role in ‘Animals’. “I used [AI] for lots of things in that movie,” he said. That was about as specific as he wanted to get. “I’m a little bit hesitant to point out what they are — or even talk about it — because in my business, we’re trying to foster the illusion of reality, right?” Affleck explained.He compared it to a magic show where the magician tells the audience how the trick works before performing it. “It sort of ruins it, right?” he said.Affleck did reveal one important detail: AI helped the production move faster, particularly in post-production. But he has not publicly listed every scene, shot or task where it was used. And he was clear about how he views the finished film.“It’s a very human movie,” Affleck said.Ben Affleck went from being scared of AI to building an AI companyBen Affleck’s interest in AI did not begin with ‘Animals’. In 2022, he founded InterPositive after spending time looking at the early development of AI and worrying about what the technology could mean for filmmakers.In the OTT giant’s announcement of its acquisition of the company on March 5, 2026, Affleck explained that he wanted to build AI specifically around the needs of filmmakers. “For artists to apply these tools towards telling the stories we dedicate our lives to, they need to be purpose-built to represent and protect all the qualities that make a great story,” he said.InterPositive developed tools designed to understand filmmaking problems such as visual logic, editorial consistency, missing shots, background replacements and incorrect lighting.The important part was how the system was designed. Affleck said the technology was built around smaller, controlled datasets and filmmaking techniques rather than performances, with safeguards intended to keep creative decisions with artists.What Ben Affleck actually thinks AI will do to HollywoodBen Affleck has not become an AI evangelist who believes technology can simply write and direct the next great movie. In fact, he has repeatedly questioned whether AI can create something meaningful from scratch.His position is more practical: if AI can take care of certain technical or repetitive parts of filmmaking, it could give filmmakers more time and freedom to focus on the actual story. That is also why his latest admission does not necessarily contradict his earlier concerns.Affleck was once worried that AI could replace filmmakers. Now he is trying to show what he believes the alternative looks like — a human-made movie where AI is another tool in the process. ‘Animals’, directed and co-written by Affleck and starring Kerry Washington, Steven Yeun and Gillian Anderson, is scheduled to release on Netflix on October 9, 2026.And for now, Affleck is leaving audiences with one unanswered question: what exactly did the AI do? articles.title: Chad Lawson on exploring his musical language in ‘Awakening: The Stillness Within’: ‘Listening became more important than talking’ - Exclusive
articles.summary: Discover how pianist Chad Lawson blends Western piano with Indian classical music in his new album \"Awakening: The Stillness Within,\" exploring the deeper meanings of stillness and healing.
articles.body: Music sure has a universal language, but its meaning is different for every musician. Recently, during an exclusive conversation with the American pianist and composer Chad Lawson, we learnt that for him, music is about exploration of stillness, presence and the spaces that exist between notes. With his latest album, ‘Awakening: The Stillness Within,’ he has tried to expand that musical language by bringing together Western piano, Indian classical instruments, mantras and healing frequencies.Chad Lawson on discovering his own musical language while bringing Western piano together with Indian classical instruments and healing frequencies“I think the biggest discovery was realising I didn't need to make the piano sound more Indian. I could let it remain a piano and become a more engaged listener myself. And while there are frequencies around this work that I find beautiful, I'm careful not to pretend I understand centuries of tradition because I spent some time recording in India. Part of respecting that tradition, for me, was also respecting the limits of my instrument,” he said while speaking to us.He added, “A bansuri can slide between two notes and live inside that space for a while. A piano can't. There are moments where I'll play two neighbouring notes, letting one arrive just before the other and releasing it a little sooner, almost trying to create the feeling of a bend. But the piano is still a fixed voice.”“That’s taught me that not everything has to become something else. Sometimes the beauty is in letting an instrument be exactly what it is. So I started paying more attention to what the piano could do naturally. Letting a note ring and fade. Playing something, leaving space around it, and waiting to hear what came back. The listening became more important than the talking,” she shared.Chad Lawson believes that respect starts with knowing what isn’t yoursOn incorporating elements of Indian classical music while respecting its cultural and musical significance, the artist said, “For me, respect starts with knowing what isn’t mine. I actually love knowing there’s something I don’t know yet.”He continued, “A raga isn't just a collection of notes you learn and then suddenly understand. Musicians can devote their entire lives to this music and still consider themselves students. I studied, listened, studied more, listened more before even landing in India, but I still walked into the studio as a beginner.”“So I wasn’t interested in trying to make their tradition fit inside what I already knew. I wanted to listen to the people who had spent their lives with it. With Purbayan Chatterjee, there is so much history and understanding behind what you're hearing. The interesting part for me wasn't trying to imitate that or tell him what I thought it should sound like. It was hearing what happened when his musical language met mine. And I couldn't stop smiling. That really became the approach throughout the record. I listened, tried to leave enough room, and trusted the musicians to bring what they knew into the music,” he mentioned.He then highlighted another very important element and said, “Credit matters too. So much of what you hear was discovered in the moment, and there are passages on this album that simply wouldn't exist without what Rasika, Purbayan, Nush and Paayal brought to it.That was the part I loved most. We could each stay ourselves completely and still make something none of us would have made alone.”Chad Lawson says healing isn't always peacefulPeople always correlate peace and healing. However, one hardly talks about the less-discussed, uncomfortable, or silent aspects of healing. Chiming in on this subject, Chad shared, “I really appreciate this question because stillness, let alone healing, isn't always peaceful. You sit down, turn everything off, and suddenly the thing you were too busy to think about all day feels like it's tapping you on the forehead. It could be grief. It could be worry. It could be something you haven't thought about in ten years. Give yourself enough quiet and things may come up that you weren't expecting.”He elaborated further with anecdotes from his own life and said, “I've meditated for years, and some mornings it's twenty minutes of thinking about groceries or what I'm doing later that day. The meditation can almost feel like a miss. But then I get up, go about my day, and that evening I do my twenty minutes again. I think that's an important part of healing. Some days nothing happens at all. But you still show up for it.”“Sometimes the uncomfortable part of healing is realizing that feeling better doesn't always mean feeling good. Sometimes you have to spend a little time with the thing you'd rather avoid. That may be part of it too,” he concluded.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Jack Black shares his powerful insights on failure, encouraging people to see it as a friend and an essential part of growth. In an interview, he highlights how overcoming the fear of failure can lead to success in various fields.
articles.body: Jack Black has built a career on being the loudest, most unpredictable, and goofiest guy in the room. ‘A Minecraft Movie’, 'School of Rock', or 'Kung Fu Panda '. He makes people laugh for a living, and he’s not scared of failing and embarrassing himself. He sees failure as a friend who teaches us what we did wrong and how to improve; he talks about how being embarrassed is okay because it’s all part of learning.Jack Black, in an interview with Access Hollywood (posted March 19, 2025) to promote 'A Minecraft Movie,' talked about how the thought of failure impedes us and how failure helps us learn.Motivational quote of the day by Jack Black reads: "What I would say to other kids or other people is don't be afraid of failure because that's the demon that will get in the way, because failure is your friend; that's when you learn."What does the quote by Jack Black really mean?Black isn't just talking about acting. He's talking about anything worth doing. Music. Writing. Starting a business. The fear of failure keeps people stuck. They don't try because they don't want to embarrass themselves. Black is saying the opposite. Go out there and bellyflop. It's fine. You'll learn something.The people who succeed aren't the ones who never fail. They're the ones who keep going after they do. Jack Black spent years doing small TV parts, and no matter the role, he didn't shy away from bringing his unique flair.How is the quote by Jack Black relevant today?This quote is relevant because it shows that the real barrier is not failure, but the fear of failure. It says it’s okay to “bellyflop” because it’s how you learn. No matter the skill or trade, you start somewhere and you make mistakes along the way, but if you don’t even try because you’re afraid of getting embarrassed, you’ll miss out.Don't let fear paralyse you. Reflect, adjust, and try again. “Failure is your friend” only works if you actually learn from it.Early life of Jack BlackThomas Jacob Black was born in Santa Monica on August 28, 1969, and raised in Hermosa Beach. His parents were satellite engineers who worked on the Hubble Space Telescope. He also attended the Crossroads School, where he excelled in drama. He did a commercial for the video game 'Pitfall!' At 13 and got hooked. He attended UCLA, but dropped out in his sophomore year to pursue entertainment. Black's Hollywood career began with small roles on prime-time television, including ‘Life Goes On’, ‘Northern Exposure’, and ‘The X-Files’.Jack Black’s rise to fameHis breakout role came in 'Shallow Hal' (2001), and after that he quickly gained leading roles in films such as 'Orange County’ (2002) and 'The Holiday' (2006). He also did voice-overs in animated features, including Zeke in ‘Ice Age’ (2002) and ‘Kung Fu Panda’. 'School of Rock' (2003) is considered the movie that made him a star. He also starred in one of his few dramatic roles as the obsessed filmmaker Carl Denham in Peter Jackson's 2005 remake of ‘King Kong.’He's been working steadily ever since. He's done family films, romantic comedies, video games, and He formed ‘Tenacious D’ with Kyle Gass, a comedy rock duo that became a cult phenomenon. articles.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard Launches Petition to Combat ‘Harassment and Cyberbullying’ After Partner Ken Urker’s Death
articles.summary: “Public figures are still human beings, and fame should never erase someone’s humanity,” she wrote
articles.body:
Gypsy Rose Blanchard's partner Ken Urker died at his Louisiana home on his 34th birthday on Oct. 1

Three days after his death, Blanchard said that she is turning her "pain into purpose" by launching a petition against "targeted harassment and cyberbullying"

She shared a Change.org petition to social media in support of Kenan's Law, an idea she created in an attempt to change "the way social-media platforms handle repeated reports of harassment"

Gypsy Rose Blanchard is fighting against "targeted harassment and cyberbullying" after the death of her partner, Ken Urker .

Urker died on Thursday, Oct. 1, at his home in Louisiana, she confirmed to PEOPLE. A spokesperson for the Lafourche Parish Sheriff's Office confirmed that officers were called to a residence in Raceland at around 6:15 p.m., and Urker, 34, was found "dead upon arrival."

Once deputies arrived, they located paraphernalia — specifically syringes and a spoon — in the bathroom next to a brown, powdery substance, according to the sheriff's office report. They also found a syringe, two shot glasses and a handgun on the nightstand next to the bed.

In a statement to PEOPLE, Blanchard said that she believed Urker overdosed, adding that he "wasn't in a good state of mind lately. He had been drinking a lot to cope."

Three days after his death, she shared a Change.org petition to social media in support of Kenan's Law, an idea she created in an attempt to change "the way social-media platforms handle repeated reports of harassment."

Blanchard tells PEOPLE that, while she hasn't yet spoken to a committee, she has contacted a lawyer out of New Orleans to help her refine the proposal.

"I only have my daughter and my voice," she wrote on Instagram. "Before his passing, Ken experienced an overwhelming amount of online scrutiny and what we believed crossed the line into targeted harassment and cyberbullying. Reports were made across multiple platforms, and far too often, the response was simply: 'No violation.' "

"Ken's passing has made me determined to turn pain into purpose," she continued. "I cannot change what happened, but I can advocate for a better system for the next person who feels like no one is listening."

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

Emphasizing that the law is "not about silencing criticism or taking away anyone's freedom of speech," Blanchard went on to remind her followers that "public figures are still human beings, and fame should never erase someone's humanity."

"Fame does not erase humanity," she concluded in her post. "A pattern cannot always be understood one post at a time. 🤍"

Hours after Urker was found dead at his Louisiana residence, Blanchard told PEOPLE that she didn't know if his death "was intentional or not."

"Ken was an amazing father and a man who was deeply loved," she said. "He will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase."

"Ken endured an unimaginable level of public scrutiny and relentless cyberbullying across social media platforms, including TikTok and Reddit," she continued. "I believe the tremendous weight of that scrutiny and harassment had a profound impact on him, and I hope his passing serves as a reminder that there is a real person behind every screen, every headline, and every comment."

Blanchard also told PEOPLE that she wants her daughter to know her father for the person he was, rather than through the lens of online commentary.

"Above all, Ken loved our daughter, Aurora. She is a beautiful reflection of his enduring spirit, and through her, a part of him will always remain with us," she said. "I will make sure she grows up knowing how deeply her father loved her and who he was beyond what strangers on the internet chose to say about him."

articles.title: 22 cases filed over noise pollution during festive celebrations in city
articles.summary: Nagpur police file 22 noise pollution cases during festivals; restrictions on high-decibel DJ systems and awareness drives intensify, rural areas report none.
articles.body: Nagpur: Nagpur city police have registered 22 cases for violations of noise-pollution norms during festive celebrations so far, while simultaneously intensifying an awareness campaign aimed at preventing excessive use of DJs, loud sound systems and other high-decibel equipment.No cases were reported in Nagpur rural police areas following intense awareness drives and meetings with mandals and organisers of festive celebrations.As per the city police data, seven cases were registered during Dahi Handi celebrations, one during Pola, three during Marbat processions, three during Ganesh idol arrival and eight during immersion. Cases were registered against organisers and sound-system operators for alleged violations of prescribed noise limits and other restrictions.The Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court has repeatedly directed the police to ensure strict implementation of noise-pollution rules. In Sept, the court had sought a report from the police after violations were reported during Dahi Handi and Marbat celebrations.Nagpur police have imposed restrictions from Sept 3 to Nov 1 covering high-powered multi-speaker DJ systems, plasma and pressure-mid sound systems and modified vehicles carrying such equipment. Police clarified that no action was taken against systems playing music within permissible noise limits.A major focus of the campaign was pre-emptive awareness. The city police conducted around 44 meetings with festival organisers, sound-system operators and other stakeholders, explaining permissible sound levels, timings and the consequences of violations.The issue also came into sharp focus during Dahi Handi celebrations. At Chhota Tajbagh Square, police registered a case against 13 persons after a DJ allegedly continued beyond the permitted time, while at Ajni Square, police recorded sound levels reaching 102.4 decibels during another Dahi Handi programme.Nagpur Rural Police also stepped up preventive measures across the district, holding meetings with Ganpati mandal organisers, DJ and sound-system operators, local representatives and members of peace committees.The rural police also reviewed festival arrangements covering Pola, Ganesh Chaturthi, Anant Chaturdashi and other celebrations. articles.title: Prick’s theatrical industrial punk is perfect for spooky season
articles.summary: If Trent Reznor studied musical theater instead of computer engineering NIN might have sounded like Kevin McMahon’s Prick.
articles.body: While deep in the recording process for The Downward Spiral, Trent Reznor lent some of his production talents to old friend Kevin McMahon, from the new wave band Lucky Pierre (which Reznor was briefly a member of). While Reznor is only credited as the producer on four tracks off Prick’s self-titled debut record, his fingerprints are all over it. But McMahon also can’t suppress his inner theater kid, which also gives the songs the sort of glammy flamboyance found on T. Rex records. Prick embraces the inherent theatricality of goth in a way that Nine Inch Nails never did. Opener “Communiqué” is a fuzzy blast of simple punk riffs with electronic sprinklings on top. McMahon’s vocals occasionally detour from the half-spoken verses that sound borrowed from a musical to full-throated Al Jourgensen-esque screams. The rough-around-the-edges production and focus on live instrumentation feel like a prototype for what Reznor would eventually revisit on With Teeth. But it’s the second track, “Riverhead” where Reznor’s influences fully rear their head (even though he is not actually credited as the producer). The vocal melodies swerve like Outside- and Earthling-era Bowie around guitars that buzz with all the digital charr of the Broken EP. Then, around the three-minute mark, comes the breakdown. It slowly builds with layers of electronic drums, mechanical chords, and loping synthetic-sounding guitar melodies. The entire back chunk could easily have been a Downward Spiral or even The Fragile B-side. These moments of richly layered production, though, are almost always immediately undermined, as with the sloppy garage-punk intro of “Tough”. It’s these moments that make Prick so charming. It’s a serious record, but it never takes itself too seriously. McMahon isn’t afraid to get goofy (“Pink panties, blue panties, yellow panties. I’m gonna wrap around your nose, oh panty-ho-hose” he sings on “Other People”) and over-the-top with his vocal performances. He’s willing to let the guitar drift out of time, the bass strings rattle, and revels in industrial lo-fi. [Media: “Animal” is perhaps the best-known track from the album, its video having received at least some MTV airplay. It combines backward melodic samples reminiscent of “Closer” and follows a similar lyrical theme: > Consent is all I need To bring out the savage in me Your scent is all I need To bring out the animal in me But where “Closer” opts for slinky disco sleaze, “Animal” is all raw shouted desire. “I Apologize” is the most scatter-brained track on the album, and for that reason, one of my favorites. It opens with awkward whip-crack-like percussion and McMahon singing slightly flat and unaffected, before briefly taking off into a jangly new wave verse that quickly morphs into a hard-rock stop in the chorus. But that’s short-lived as well. The second verse is all “Space Oddity”-era Bowie acoustic strums, then there’s a solo that sounds like an arcade machine on the verge of meltdown. That then drops into a Ministry-esque dirge of layered guitars and screams. The song then returns to the chorus, but keeps adding elements until it’s stuffed to capacity and collapses on itself. Prick’s self-titled record has plenty in common with other ‘90s industrial acts. But McMahon is clearly having a lot more fun than many of his contemporaries, and that helps elevate it above the myriad Nine Inch Nails wannabes out there. Prick is available on most major streaming services, including Apple Music, Spotify, Qobuz, Deezer, and YouTube Music.

articles.summary: On the cusp of the studio's merger with Paramount, Warner Bros.' 'Digger' flopped in its opening weekend, handing Tom Cruise one of the worst debuts of
articles.body: On the cusp of the studio's merger with Paramount, Warner Bros.' 'Digger' flopped in its opening weekend, handing Tom Cruise one of the worst debuts of his career and serving as a bitter final note for Warner Bros. as a standalone studio.Tom Cruise' 'Digger' flops at box office'Digger', one of the year's biggest gambles, directed by Alejandro G. Inarritu, grossed a paltry USD 8 million domestically. Cruise is typically a big draw overseas, but international sales, USD 12 million from 74 markets, were also weak.After reviews so bad that Warner Bros. opted to run "decide for yourself" ads, estimates for "Digger" had been revised down over the past week.It's a painfully rough start for a movie that cost at least USD 125 million to make. Reports have pegged the production budget closer to USD 150 million. The marketing spend is estimated at another USD 100 million.'Digger' had been positioned as a potential awards-season heavyweight, dated almost exactly the same as Warner Bros.' 'One Battle After Another' was last year. The film is a similarly politically charged release that handed a large budget to a top filmmaker working from an original story.But this big swing by Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group co-chairs Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy won't pay off as well as 'One Battle After Another'. It grossed USD 213.2 million worldwide and, more importantly, won Best Picture at the Academy Awards.'Digger' flops amid Hollywood transformationThe disappointing opening comes just as Paramount Skydance is closing its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. After U.S. District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin on Wednesday approved the USD 110 billion deal, Paramount said it would close the merger on Tuesday.In a flush year for Hollywood, Warner Bros. has failed to get one film to USD 100 million domestically, though its December release, 'Dune: Part III', will easily cross that. De Luca and Abdy are expected to depart Warner Bros. this week. Mass layoffs are anticipated to follow.Critics (51% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes) slammed 'Digger' as a strained climate change farce, though Cruise's over-the-top performance was received more warmly. Audiences agreed, giving it a "C+" CinemaScore.Cruise has spent most of the last decade starring in 'Mission: Impossible' movies and 'Top Gun: Maverick', both franchises that have allowed him to remain a top action hero into his 60s. The 64-year-old's last major box-office disappointment was 2017's 'The Mummy', which grossed USD 409.2 million worldwide on a USD 195 million budget.To help sell 'Digger', Cruise pulled out all the stops. He even granted his first lengthy magazine interview in years.'Verity' tops box officeNo. 1 in North American theaters instead went to Amazon MGM's 'Verity', extending the streak for Colleen Hoover adaptations at the box office. It debuted with USD 32.6 million. The film, directed by Michael Showalter, stars Dakota Johnson as a writer hired to ghostwrite a book series by an incapacitated author (Anne Hathaway).The film's success has helped leading lady Anne add a page to the record books, by scorring three No. 1 films in a year, the most for any actress. The actress first topped the box office early this year, with the release of 'The Devil Wears Prada', she also starred in 'The Odyssey'.'Avengers: Endgame' retakes all-time crownLast weekend's top film, 'Avengers Endgame: Encore', slid to seventh place with USD 4.4 million domestically and USD 14.4 million overseas. But the Marvel re-release's second week allowed 'Endgame' to just nudge ahead of 'Avatar' to reclaim the title of highest grossing film of all time, not accounting for inflation. The two films have traded spots in recent years with re-releases. 'Endgame' now tallies USD 2.9255 billion, while 'Avatar' has USD 2.9237 billion.'Resident Evil', 'Heart of the Beast' and 'Primetime' take top 5 spotsThe rest of the top-sellers in cinemas over the weekend were holdovers: Zach Cregger's video game adaptation 'Resident Evil' for Sony Pictures; Lance Oppenheim's A24 drama 'Primetime', with Robert Pattinson as 'To Catch a Predator' host Chris Hansen; and Paramount's 'Heart of the Beast', starring Brad Pitt as a retired veteran who treks through the Alaskan wilderness with his combat dog after a plane crash.In its third week, 'Resident Evil' came in second with USD 12.5 million. 'Heart of the Beast' followed with USD 11 million. And 'Primetime' collected USD 8 million in its second weekend.Top 10 movies at North American box officeWith final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak:1. articles.summary: Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Endgame’ has officially reclaimed the title of the highest-grossing film of all time!
articles.body: Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Endgame’ has officially reclaimed the title of the highest-grossing film of all time! The film on Sunday, following its theatrical re-release as ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’, surpassed James Cameron’s ‘Avatar’, thus officially reclaiming the box office crown.'Avengers: Endgame' becomes highest-grossing film of all timeAs per box office reports, the film's total haul now stands at approximately USD 2.9255 billion worldwide, edging past ‘Avatar’, which has a lifetime global total of around USD 2.9237 billion.The Marvel blockbuster’s latest boost came from ‘Endgame: Encore’, which added approximately USD 126 million to its worldwide haul. After a strong opening re-release, earning approximately USD 86 million worldwide, the film, however, slipped to seventh place at the domestic box office in its second weekend, earning USD 4.4 million in North America and USD 14.4 million internationally.Despite the drop, the additional earnings were enough for ‘Endgame’ to narrowly overtake ‘Avatar’ and reclaim the global box office crown.Marvel Studios thanks fansMarvel Studios celebrated the milestone on social media, writing, “Thank you for assembling to make Avengers: Endgame the biggest movie of all time. We love you 3000.”The Russo Brothers thank fans for making 'Endgame' the number 1 filmThe Russo brothers also shared a video message to thank fans for their support. "Thank you for coming back to theaters for Endgame Encore and making Endgame the #1 film of all time. To every fan who’s been part of this journey for the last seven years, we love you 3000," they said in a social media post.'Endgame' and 'Avatar' continue to trade placesThe battle between the two blockbusters has been one of the closest in modern box office history. ‘Avengers: Endgame’ initially overtook ‘Avatar’ in 2019, becoming the highest-grossing film in history before Cameron’s film regained the crown following a 2021 re-release in China.‘Avatar’ subsequently added further to its worldwide total through another global theatrical re-release in September 2022, ahead of the release of ‘Avatar: The Way of Water’The film's box office success comes as Marvel Studios builds anticipation for ‘Avengers: Doomsday’, which is scheduled to hit cinemas on December 18, 2026. articles.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard launches anti-bullying campaign after sudden death of partner
articles.summary: Gypsy Rose Blanchard says Ken Urker faced targeted cyberbullying before his death and is now pushing Kenan's Law to reform social media platforms.
articles.body: Gypsy Rose Blanchard is turning her "pain into purpose" after the sudden death of her partner, Kenan "Ken" Urker. Urker died at his Louisiana home on his birthday Thursday, Oct. 1, Fox News Digital confirmed. He was 34. Blanchard, 35, explained that Urker experienced "an overwhelming amount of online scrutiny" prior to his death, and pleaded with her social media followers to sign an anti-bullying petition in his honor. GYPSY ROSE BLANCHARD’S PARTNER, KEN URKER, FOUND DEAD INSIDE HIS LOUISIANA HOME: SHERIFF "I only have my daughter and my voice," Blanchard shared on social media over the weekend. "In honor of Ken, I am asking for your support for Kenan’s Law." "Before his passing, Ken experienced an overwhelming amount of online scrutiny and what we believed crossed the line into targeted harassment and cyberbullying." Blanchard claimed that "reports were made across multiple platforms," but noted that "far too often, the response was simply: 'No violation.'" "Kenan’s Law is about changing the way social-media platforms handle repeated reports of harassment," she wrote. "One post viewed alone may not tell the whole story—but hundreds of posts, videos and comments directed at one person can reveal a pattern that deserves meaningful review." CHAD LOWE'S DAUGHTER MABEL SHARES HEARTBREAKING TRIBUTE TO LATE SISTER FIONA, 13 "This is not about silencing criticism or taking away anyone’s freedom of speech. Public figures can and should be criticized. But public figures are still human beings, and fame should never erase someone’s humanity. She added, "Ken’s passing has made me determined to turn pain into purpose. I cannot change what happened, but I can advocate for a better system for the next person who feels like no one is listening." Blanchard asked followers to "sign and share" the petition, before noting, "Fame does not erase humanity. A pattern cannot always be understood one post at a time." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "He was not in a good state of mind lately." The Lafourche Parish Sheriff's Office confirmed Urker was found dead inside his Louisiana home Thursday after loved ones requested a welfare check. Anita Blanchard told authorities that she and her husband, who is Gypsy Rose Blanchard's half-brother, went to the 34-year-old's home and spotted Urker lying unconscious from an outside window, according to an incident report. A man accompanying Anita Blanchard and her husband then entered the house through a window and found Urker, who was not breathing and cold to the touch, according to the report. Investigators recovered syringes and a spoon next to a brown powdery substance in the bathroom, as well as a handgun, two shot glasses, and a syringe on a nightstand next to the bed, the report states. FORMER DISNEY TEEN STAR EXPOSES CHILLING WARNING SIGNS OF PREDATORY BEHAVIOR IN HOLLYWOOD "I was true to myself then," Humperdinck continued. "And I avoided all that, but I went through hell with that sort of thing." Humperdinck described the experience as refusing to participate in the industry's "casting couch." HARVEY WEINSTEIN SENTENCED TO 15 YEARS IN PRISON FOR 2006 SEX CRIME IN NEW YORK "Casting couch, it's called the casting couch, right?" he said."Not in a Hollywood way, but in an agent's way, you know." articles.body: "The Real Housewives of New Jersey" star Teresa Giudice's daughter Milania Giudice reflected on her bond with her sister Gabriella in a heartfelt birthday tribute months after her older sibling reportedly called 911 on her during a family dispute. In May, Milania, 20, was arrested and charged with simple assault following a reported domestic dispute at Teresa's home in Montville Township, New Jersey. "You're genuinely one of the smartest people I know, and I'm so proud of the person you are," she continued. "I've put you through a lot over the years, and I know I haven't always made being my sister easy, but you've always been there for me, accepted me, and loved me through everything," Milania added. articles.body: Frank Grillo sent social media abuzz with speculation surrounding the cast of 'Man of Tomorrow'.The actor's post repost of a fan poster, sent social media into a frenzy over Adria Arjona’s mystery role in the DC Universe. According to the poster, featuring the cast, the actress was pictured as Wonder Woman, aka Diana Prince alongside Aaron Pierre as John Stewart. articles.title: ‘I am people-made star,’ says Sivakarthikeyan; 'Seyon' actor opens up on criticism, sends strong message to fans at Chennai gathering
articles.summary: Sivakarthikeyan’s latest interaction with his fan club administrators has created a buzz beyond the usual fan event.
articles.body: Sivakarthikeyan’s latest interaction with his fan club administrators has created a buzz beyond the usual fan event. The actor met more than 2,000 administrators from different parts of Tamil Nadu at a gathering near Porur in Chennai. The event brought together state, district, city, union and area-level representatives in an organised setup. The venue itself attracted attention, with its entrance designed like a grand fort. The fans also turned up in similar white shirts, giving the gathering a strong political-meet-like appearance. However, Sivakarthikeyan’s speech focused more on his bond with people, personal values, and the purpose behind the gathering.Sivakarthikeyan says ‘I am a people-made star’ in candid speechAddressing the gathering, Sivakarthikeyan opened up about his journey and the support he has received from his fans. As reported by News 18, the actor made it clear that he does not see his success as something he achieved alone. “I am not a self-made star. I am a people-made star. This stardom would not be possible without the people,” he said. Sivakarthikeyan also spoke about the criticism he faces and asked his supporters not to get distracted by negative comments. “Those who criticise will keep criticising. We should continue doing our work like a river that creates its own path,” he said. He added that the gathering was built on mutual affection and urged everyone to remain clear about its purpose.Sivakarthikeyan urges fans to put family first and read booksThe actor also used the occasion to share a few personal thoughts with his fan administrators. Stressing the importance of family, Sivakarthikeyan said, “Family should always come first. Whatever we do, we should never forget our family.” He also urged them to develop the habit of reading and spend at least 15 minutes with books every day. “Please read books for at least 15 minutes every day. If you want to stay away from social media, books are a good alternative,” he said. His fan clubs have also been involved in welfare activities, including blood donation drives, educational support and other forms of assistance. After the meeting, Sivakarthikeyan visited the book stall arranged at the venue and interacted with the organisers, reinforcing his message about reading and staying focused on meaningful activities.Sivakarthikeyan shares 'Seyon' updateThe event also brought an update on Sivakarthikeyan’s upcoming film 'Seyon.' The actor revealed that around 60 per cent of the film has been completed. He described it as a mix of action and entertainment and promised that it would cater to his fans’ expectations. The film is now expected to arrive for Pongal 2027, instead of the earlier October 2026 plan.Directed by Sivakumar Murugesan, 'Seyon' features Raj B Shetty, Bhagyashri Borse, Seeman, Bala Saravanan, Arul Doss and Singampuli alongside Sivakarthikeyan. articles.summary: Sanjay Leela Bhansali and Alia Bhatt could be heading for another collaboration after 'Love & War', with the actor-director duo reportedly discussing the
articles.body: Sanjay Leela Bhansali and Alia Bhatt could be heading for another collaboration after 'Love & War', with the actor-director duo reportedly discussing the revival of their long-shelved project Inshallah. The film, which was originally announced in 2019 with Salman Khan and Alia Bhatt in the lead, never went on floors after Salman’s exit and subsequent creative differences with Bhansali. Now, according to a report by Mid-Day, Inshallah may be back on the filmmaker’s table, but not necessarily in the form audiences were promised seven years ago. Bhansali and Bhatt are said to be exploring a substantially reworked version of the romantic drama, with the script expected to undergo significant changes before the casting is locked.Sanjay Leela Bhansali and Alia Bhatt discuss reviving 'Inshallah'If the discussions materialise, 'Inshallah' would mark another collaboration between Bhansali and Alia after 'Gangubai Kathiawadi' and 'Love & War'. The two are reportedly considering revisiting the film following their experience of working together on the upcoming period drama.According to Mid-Day, the proposed version will retain the basic premise of the story but will be substantially reworked. A source cited by the publication explained that the project is not being approached as a straightforward continuation of the version announced in 2019. Instead, Bhansali and Bhatt are said to be looking at the material afresh and giving the love story a new treatment.The development could potentially give 'Inshallah' a second life after the ambitious project remained in limbo for years.'Inshallah' was originally announced with Salman Khan and Alia Bhatt'Inshallah' was one of the most anticipated Bollywood projects announced in 2019, bringing together Salman Khan and Bhansali for the first time in two decades while also pairing Salman with Alia on screen. However, the project was eventually shelved following creative differences between Salman and Bhansali. The filmmaker subsequently moved ahead with 'Gangubai Kathiawadi', which starred Alia in the titular role.The film's revival has remained a subject of speculation over the years, particularly because Bhansali has continued to express interest in ambitious, character-driven stories while Alia has become one of the filmmaker's key collaborators.Will Shah Rukh Khan be part of 'Inshallah'?Earlier this year, there was speculation that Shah Rukh Khan could step in as the male lead if 'Inshallah' was revived. However, according to the latest information cited by Mid-Day, no casting decision has been taken yet. The reason is reportedly straightforward: Bhansali wants the screenplay to be locked before deciding who will headline the film. With Salman currently committed to other projects like Raj and DK's film and Shah Rukh yet to finalise his next project after 'King', the filmmaker could also consider a younger actor depending on what the reworked script demands.This means that while Alia appears to be central to the revival discussions, the male lead remains an open question.Why 'Inshallah' could look very different this timeThe biggest change could be in the film's writing. Rather than simply replacing Salman with another actor, Bhansali and Alia are reportedly discussing a version that substantially revisits the original material.The story is expected to retain its core but receive a contemporary treatment, with the characters and narrative potentially being reshaped around the actor who eventually comes on board.For Bhansali, the approach is in keeping with his tendency to prioritise the script and character arcs before finalising his ensemble. It also gives Inshallah an opportunity to evolve beyond the version that was announced in 2019.Alia Bhatt’s current work slateAlia Bhatt recently headlined Yash Raj Films' Alpha, the female-led action film set within the YRF Spy Universe, alongside Sharvari. The film was released theatrically on July 3, 2026. Bhatt is also gearing up for Sanjay Leela Bhansali's 'Love & War', which reunites her with Ranbir Kapoor and also stars Vicky Kaushal. The film is currently in post-production and is scheduled for release in January 2027.Beyond these projects, Alia's announced slate includes Sohum Shah's 'Tumbbad 2' alongside Shah and Nawazuddin Siddiqui.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Culture legacy could see Bradford Mela and Bingley festivals return
articles.summary: Plans to revive the Bradford Mela and create a new Bingley festival look to be moving forward.
articles.body:
Plans for two major Bradford arts festivals look set to move forward as part of the continuing legacy of the UK City of Culture year.

The creation of a new music festival in Bingley, and the return of the original Bradford Mela, had already been hinted at by officials, and a council report confirms they will be funded with millions of pounds set aside for the Bradford 2025 follow-on programme.

The report also says the size of the local visitor economy soared to more than £1bn in 2025, the first time that milestone has been reached.

But it raises questions over the future of the Bradford Culture Company Ltd, with the council considering "whether, and in what form, it should continue".

The report says: "The principal strategic risk is ensuring that the momentum, partnerships, profile, participation and investment created through Bradford 2025 are converted into sustained long-term benefit."

The report to the decision-making executive confirms that the council still has £4.269m set aside specifically for Bradford 2025 and its legacy work over the next three financial years to 2030.

It comes from a five-year commitment of £1.423m a year agreed and rubber-stamped by the previous Labour-run administration in 2022.

The broader Bradford 2025 bid had received cross-party backing earlier.

The report says the remaining money will help keep cultural events going across the district and develop new ones, including "plans for a new major music festival in Bingley and the reintroduction of Bradford Mela".

However, it gives no details of venues or individual budgets and does not say who would run the events.

Bingley has previously been home to major music festivals, including Bingley Music Live and the later, independently run Bingley Weekender.

Bradford Mela, a huge South Asian festival which attracted crowds of more than 100,000 in its heyday, was also a long-standing fixture in the city's events calendar, but effectively ended in 2013 following cancellations in 2007 and 2012 which were attributed to bad weather .

The two festivals form part of wider cultural legacy plans with the report, to be presented at a meeting on Thursday, explaining that in 2027-28, the annual amount available to cultural organisations receiving regular council support will rise from £590,000 to £700,000.

Another pot for individual projects will more than double, from about £85,000 to £200,000 a year.

More than 20 projects have also been offered grants for work on buildings, spaces and equipment, it says.

The pledges come despite a separate decision by the Reform UK-led council to divert £400,000 of arts funding towards the reopening of a tip in Keighley, with a petition opposing the move having gathered more than 500 signatures so far.

A key unanswered question raised in the executive report is what happens to Bradford Culture Company Ltd (BCCL) after March 2027.

The organisation delivered Bradford 2025 and is now running the follow-on programme.

But no decision has yet been made on whether the company itself will continue beyond 31 March 2027.

The report says the council and BCCL are "actively considering the company's future role and operating model", including "whether, and in what form, it should continue".

For now, says the report, it is continuing work started during Bradford 2025, including volunteering, creative health projects and support for people working in the arts.

The report says 2025 saw 10.6 million day visits, worth an estimated £719m, while 1.53 million visitors stayed in Bradford for a holiday or short break.

The visitor economy is also estimated to have supportded almost 9,000 full-time equivalent jobs.

The report stresses that the whole £1.08bn cannot simply be credited to Bradford 2025, however it does "demonstrate the scale of the opportunity to convert increased profile and visitation into sustained economic benefit".

It adds the continuing legacy work will further "help... to increase footfall, attract national attention and strengthen Bradford's position as a major cultural destination and producer".
