articles.title: Supreme Court slams Rajpal Yadav for not complying with its orders of depositing Rs 5 crore in cheque bounce case, the actor gives only Rs 50 lakhs
articles.summary: Rajpal Yadav has been in legal trouble for Rs 9 crore debt case and was even sentenced three months jail by the Supreme Court.
articles.body: Rajpal Yadav has been in legal trouble for Rs 9 crore debt case and was even sentenced three months jail by the Supreme Court. The dispute dates back to 2010, when Rajpal Yadav borrowed close to Rs. 5 crore from a Delhi-based firm to finance his directorial debut, 'Ata Pata Laapata'. The comedy film failed to perform as expected at the box office, leaving the actor unable to generate sufficient returns to repay the loan. Over time, the outstanding amount reportedly increased because of interest and additional charges, eventually reaching nearly Rs 9 crore.As per the hearing on September 15, the court had given interim relief and exempted from jail and was asked to deposit Rs 5 crore. However, as per the hearing which took place today, October 5, the actor has not complied by the court's orders. Law Beat tweeted, "Supreme Court comes down heavily on Actor Rajpal Yadav for not complying with its directions to deposit Rs 5 Crore in Cheque Bounce Cases against him.Yadav's counsel: A photocopy of demand draft of Rs 50 lakhs is placed before court...it will reach Delhi by tomorrow..CJI Surya Kant: ₹50 lakhs? articles.title: Lata Mangeshkar never married, but one man remained close to her for decades: The story behind their private bond
articles.summary: Lata Mangeshkar spent most of her life keeping her personal relationships away from the public eye.
articles.body: Lata Mangeshkar spent most of her life keeping her personal relationships away from the public eye. But one name remained closely associated with her for decades: Raj Singh Dungarpur, the Rajasthan royal, first-class cricketer and former BCCI president. The two shared a close bond that began in the late 1950s and continued for years. Neither ever publicly described the relationship in detail. Dungarpur, however, spoke about it in a rare interview with Mid-Day, while Mangeshkar gave an equally guarded response when asked about the man often described in the media as her romantic partner. Their story has since been repeatedly described as a love story that never ended in marriage. But the most reliable accounts are quieter: the two came from different backgrounds, were deeply attached to their families and remained close despite never marrying.How Lata Mangeshkar met Raj Singh DungarpurDungarpur himself recalled meeting Mangeshkar in 1959, when he had come to Bombay to study law. He told Mid-Day that he had told Dilip Sardesai's first cousin, Sopan Sardesai, that he could not live without playing cricket. Sardesai directed him to a Walkeshwar house where Lata's brother and his friends played tennis-ball cricket. “I said I'm not bothered by who plays, but I have to be there,” Dungarpur recalled. At the time, Mangeshkar was recording extensively and Dungarpur said he was not particularly interested in meeting her. He would play cricket and return to his sister's house in Napean Sea Road. That changed when he was invited upstairs.“But her family must have discussed that I had come, so she said, ‘We must offer him a cup of tea.’ I was invited to come up,” he recalled in the interview to Mid-Day. He described her as “utterly charming” and remembered that she came to see him off and gave him her car. She later invited him and his brother for dinner. “That’s how I started to know her. I went for a couple of her recordings and so on,” he said.From friendship to a bond that lasted decadesDungarpur became a regular presence in Mangeshkar's life. Their association was also noted in contemporary accounts. Dungarpur was Mangeshkar's “only enduring companion” and accompanied her on foreign tours and helped with dates and professional dealings, as reported by India Today. The report also said both were uncomfortable with their companionship being discussed publicly. Later reports described their relationship as romantic, but Mangeshkar herself rarely addressed those reports. In a later interview with Hindustan Times, she was asked about the role of love in her life and who the “lucky man” was. Her answer remained deliberately private. “There are some things only for the heart to know. Let me keep it that way,” she said.Why did Lata Mangeshkar and Raj Singh Dungarpur never marry?This is where much of the story has been surrounded by speculation. Later reports have claimed that Dungarpur's royal family objected to the relationship and that Mangeshkar's family preferred a Marathi match for her. Dungarpur himself gave a more measured explanation. Asked about their relationship in the Mid-Day interview, he said: “This is a very personal matter. But we came from different backgrounds. The '60s were very different.” He added that both were perhaps very attached to their respective families. “It was one of those things that just didn't happen,” he said. But he was clear that the absence of marriage had not ended their bond. “But that has neither enhanced the relationship, nor has it reduced. She is the treasure house of my admiration and affection and I continue to be in touch with her,” Dungarpur said.Lata had another explanation for never marryingMangeshkar also spoke about marriage at different points in her life, although she did not publicly confirm or deny the details of her relationship with Dungarpur. In a 1999 interview, she was asked why she had never married. “I never got time to think about it,” she said, explaining that she had started working at 13 and had taken responsibility for supporting her family after her father's death. She said marriage simply did not occur to her. Asked whether she felt lonely or regretted remaining single, she replied: “No. I never feel lonely and I don't regret it. I am happy the way I am.”In another Hindustan Times interview published years later, she again said the thought of being unmarried or becoming a mother had never really crossed her mind because she was surrounded by her close-knit family. She also said she believed that birth, marriage and death were destined.Their bond continued despite never marryingDungarpur was not known only because of his association with Mangeshkar. Born in 1935, he was the youngest son of Maharawal Lakshman Singhji, the ruler of Dungarpur. He played first-class cricket for Rajasthan and Central Zone between 1955 and 1971. Dungarpur remained unmarried. He died in Mumbai in September 2009, aged 73. The BCCI's annual report records his death on September 12, 2009. Mangeshkar continued to live and work in the world of music for more than a decade after his death. She died in February 2022 at the age of 92. For a relationship that attracted decades of speculation, that remains the clearest account from one of the two people who lived it. And Mangeshkar's own words remain equally telling: “There are some things only for the heart to know. Let me keep it that way.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Shefali Shah opens up on her first marriage with Harsh Chhaya in her memoir: 'Haven't named anyone but nobody is prepared for a divorce, nothing to hide about it'
articles.summary: Shefali Shah has opened up about her first marriage to actor Harsh Chhaya in her new memoir-in-essays, ‘The Audacity of Being’.
articles.body: Shefali Shah has opened up about her first marriage to actor Harsh Chhaya in her new memoir-in-essays, ‘The Audacity of Being’. While the actor has chosen to keep the details of the relationship private, she has written about the emotional experience of watching a marriage fall apart and what follows when a couple is unprepared for the possibility of divorce.Shefali made it clear that she has deliberately stayed away from naming people or discussing the specifics of what happened in her first marriage. “I’m not naming anyone in the book. I’m not even getting into what happened or didn’t happen. I’m just talking about what happens on a general scale when people get married and nobody’s prepared for a divorce," she said in an interview with Indian Express.Shefali was earlier married to Harsh Chhaya. The actor later married filmmaker-producer Vipul Amrutlal Shah in 2000, and the couple has two sons, Aryaman and Maurya.According to Shefali, people often enter marriage imagining that it will inevitably lead to a happy ending. However, life does not always follow that script. She said, “the idea of a happily-ever-after”, adding, “Marriage may not necessarily pan out the way it is. And then, you just have no option but to deal with it.”The actor was also asked about the openness with which she has approached her personal life in the book, particularly while writing about the end of her first marriage. Shefali said she did not feel there was anything she needed to conceal, explaining, “There was nothing to really hide about. I think I’ve written about it very respectfully. I’m just talking about any marriage falling off the brink. There’s an entire thing about when you realise your marriage is falling apart. So it’s, I think, about the failure of a relationship.”However, her book goes well beyond her experiences with marriage and divorce. ‘The Audacity of Being’ explores love, heartbreak, friendships, community, ageing as an actor in Bollywood, creative insecurities, body image and the challenges of parenting.Shefali has described the book as “a sort of memoir”. When the book was announced, she had said, “Nothing in my life warrants a memoir. And yet, I chose to tell a story only I have the copyright to. I don’t promise an ingenious book, but what I do promise is absolute honesty.”With a career spanning more than three decades, Shefali has built a reputation for choosing varied and layered roles across films and streaming projects. Her work includes ‘Satya’, ‘Monsoon Wedding’, ‘Dil Dhadakne Do’, ‘Jalsa’ and ‘Darlings’, apart from the Emmy-winning series ‘Delhi Crime’.The actor is also conscious that putting personal experiences into the public domain inevitably invites interpretation. Reflecting on that aspect of being open about her life, she said, “When you put yourself out there in the public domain, whether it’s on camera or when you are writing something, or even on Instagram, people will have a point of view.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Quote of the day by John Travolta: ‘I think you learn by your failures, and you learn by your mistakes, but you don't take them to heart…you rise above it all,' the ‘Grease’ star’s words of wisdom on how to move past your failures in life
articles.summary: Inspiring insights from John Travolta on learning from failures and moving past mistakes, along with a glimpse into his life and career ups and downs.
articles.body: Hollywood icon John Travolta has had his fair share of failures and hardships in life. From facing a major career slump in the 1980s to losing his son and his wife, he has been through a lot. However, he continues to rise above and keeps his life open to opportunities. Failure is an inevitable part of the human journey, but how we respond to it defines our path forward.The quote of the day reads, "I think you learn by your failures, and you learn by your mistakes, but you don't take them to heart, because as soon as you do, you die a little bit. So you get through that, the best you can, by living life fully and using the spirit of other people to feed you, and you feed them, and you rise above it all that way.”What does John Travolta’s quote of the day mean?John Travolta shared these thoughts on December 20, 1998, while he was talking to James Lipton for his ‘Inside the Actors Studio’ interview. During the interview, the actor spoke about his career's dramatic ups and downs and how he was a big commercial success for a couple of years; however, around the 1980s, he went through a major slump, which was later revived by his film, ‘Pulp Fiction,’ with Uma Thurman.Travolta’s quote is about understanding the difference between learning an objective lesson and internalizing shame. Failures provide us the space to grow and get better as a person, but taking them "to heart" turns something temporary into a permanent personal flaw. Making a mistake means something didn't work out; taking it to heart means believing you are a failure even though there is no need to internalize those emotions.If you constantly end up taking setbacks to heart, it chips away at your confidence, enthusiasm, and willingness to take future risks and often brings your confidence in yourself and your skills down.Rather than living in the past, Travolta emphasizes that it is important to live your life to the fullest, no matter how many mistakes you have made, because at the end of the day, they are nothing but stepping stones that you need to use to get to your future goal. These mistakes are lessons that need to remain in the past. The solution to failure is not overanalyzing things but instead actively engaging with life. At its core, the quote talks about how life continues regardless of past mistakes. Choosing to live fully keeps your focus on present opportunities rather than past regrets.Who is John TravoltaJohn Joseph Travolta was born on February 18, 1954, in Englewood, New Jersey. Travolta is the youngest of six siblings and grew up in a house that was heavily inspired by Hollywood. His mother, Helen Cecilia, was an actress and singer with the radio vocal group The Sunshine Sisters before she started teaching drama and English at a high school. His father, Salvatore Travolta, played semi-professional football before he started his own tire business.About John Travolta’s careerTravolta rose to fame playing Vinnie Barbarino on the TV sitcom ‘Welcome Back, Kotter’ from 1975 to 1979. He transitioned into a major film star with back-to-back blockbusters such as ‘Saturday Night Fever’ (1977), which defined the disco era and earned him an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor.Other than that, one of his most popular works to date remains ‘Grease’ (1978), in which he played the iconic Danny Zuko alongside Olivia Newton-John. During the 1980s, the actor faced a major slump in his career and did not score any high-end blockbusters up until the 90s, when his career kicked off all over again. Travolta made a dramatic comeback when Quentin Tarantino cast him as hitman Vincent Vega in ‘Pulp Fiction’ (1994), which helped get him his second Oscar nomination.Some of his other major roles over the years include ‘Get Shorty’ (1995), ‘Face/Off’ (1997), ‘Primary Colors’ (1998), ‘Hairspray’ (2007), and ‘The People v. O. J. Simpson: American Crime Story’ (2016).Beyond his on-screen prowess, the actor is best known for being a certified private pilot and aviation enthusiast who owns multiple aircraft. He created his home near an airfield so that he could park his private planes in his backyard. articles.title: On cusp of merger, ‘Digger’ bombs for Warner Bros., ‘Verity’ takes No. 1 at box office
articles.summary: On the cusp of the studio’s merger with Paramount, Warner Bros.’ “Digger” flopped in its opening weekend, handing Tom Cruise one of the worst debuts of his career and serving as a bitter final note for Warner Bros.
articles.body: NEW YORK — On the cusp of the studio’s merger with Paramount, Warner Bros.’ “Digger” flopped in its opening weekend, handing Tom Cruise one of the worst debuts of his career and serving as a bitter final note for Warner Bros. as a standalone studio. No. 1 in North American theaters instead went to Amazon MGM’s “Verity,” extending the streak for Colleen Hoover adaptations at the box office. It debuted with $32.6 million. The film, directed by Michael Showalter, stars Dakota Johnson as a writer hired to ghostwrite a book series by an incapacitated author (Anne Hathaway). But all eyes were on how “Digger,” one of the year’s biggest gambles, would perform. Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s critically panned satire grossed a paltry $8 million domestically. Cruise is typically a big draw overseas, but international sales, $12 million from 74 markets, were also weak. After reviews so bad that Warner Bros. opted to run “decide for yourself” ads, estimates for “Digger” had been revised down over the past week. It’s a painfully rough start for a movie that cost at least $125 million to make. Reports have pegged the production budget closer to $150 million. The marketing spend is estimated at another $100 million. “Digger” had been positioned as a potential awards-season heavyweight, dated almost exactly the same as Warner Bros.’ “One Battle After Another” was last year. “Digger” is a similarly politically charged release that handed a large budget to a top filmmaker working from an original story. But this big swing by Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group co-chairs Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy won’t pay off as well as “One Battle After Another.” It grossed $213.2 million worldwide and, more importantly, won best picture at the Academy Awards. ‘Digger’ flops at a moment of Hollywood transformation The disappointing opening comes just as Paramount Skydance is closing its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. After U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín on Wednesday approved the $110 billion deal, Paramount said it would close the merger on Tuesday. In a flush year for Hollywood, Warner Bros. has failed to get one film to $100 million domestically, though its December release, “Dune: Part III,” will easily cross that. De Luca and Abdy are expected to depart Warner Bros. this week. Mass layoffs are anticipated to follow. “‘Digger’ collapsed this weekend and the new management of the combined Paramount and Warner Bros., David Ellison and Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg, will soon decide what kind of movies they want from WB,” wrote David A. Gross, a film consultant who publishes a newsletter on box office figures. “Paramount does not have a recent history of making big, auteur-driven films like this — that strategy appears to be over and out.” Critics (51% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes) slammed “Digger” as a strained climate change farce, though Cruise’s over-the-top performance was received more warmly. Audiences agreed, giving it a “C+” CinemaScore. Cruise has spent most of the last decade starring in “Mission: Impossible” movies and “Top Gun: Maverick,” both franchises that have allowed him to remain a top action hero into his 60s. The 64-year-old’s last major box-office disappointment was 2017’s “The Mummy,” which grossed $409.2 million worldwide on a $195 million budget. To help sell “Digger,” Cruise pulled out all the stops. He even granted his first lengthy magazine interview in years. ‘Avengers: Endgame’ retakes all-time crown Last weekend’s top film, “Avengers Endgame: Encore,” slid to seventh place with $4.4 million domestically and $14.4 million overseas. But the Marvel re-release’s second week allowed “Endgame” to just nudge ahead of “Avatar” to reclaim the title of highest grossing film ever, not accounting for inflation. The two films have traded spots in recent years with re-releases. “Endgame” now tallies $2.9255 billion, while “Avatar” has $2.9237 billion. The rest of the top-sellers in cinemas over the weekend were holdovers: Zach Cregger’s video game adaptation “Resident Evil” for Sony Pictures; Lance Oppenheim’s A24 drama “Primetime,” with Robert Pattinson as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen; and Paramount’s “Heart of the Beast,” starring Brad Pitt as a retired veteran who treks through the Alaskan wilderness with his combat dog after a plane crash. In its third week, “Resident Evil” came in second with $12.5 million. “Heart of the Beast” followed with $11 million. And “Primetime” collected $8 million in its second weekend. Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “Verity,” $32.6 million. 2. “Resident Evil,” $12.5 million. 3. “Heart of the Beast,” $11 million. 4. “Primetime,” $8 million. 5. “Digger,” $8 million. 6. “Forgotten Island,” $7.2 million. 7. “Avengers: Endgame: Encore,” $4.4 million. 8. “Drishyam: The Conclusion,” $2.7 million. 9. “Practical Magic 2,” $2.7 million. 10. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” $2.5 million.

articles.title: Raju Kher recalls his bad phase where he sold off his house, brother Anupam Kher didn't help him: 'We took him for granted thinking that he doesn't have any problems'
articles.summary: Actor-director Raju Kher has opened up about one of the most difficult phases of his career and how it changed his relationship with his elder brother,
articles.body: Actor-director Raju Kher has opened up about one of the most difficult phases of his career and how it changed his relationship with his elder brother, veteran actor Anupam Kher. Recalling the events of around 2000, Raju said he had once expected financial support from Anupam, only to later realise that his brother was also dealing with his own struggles at the time.Raju recalled how he had sold his house and invested the money in a programme for a new television channel. He eventually moved into a rented flat after the channel unexpectedly shut down.“There was a time when I was going through a bad phase. I had sold my house because a new channel was coming, so I had bought a flat elsewhere. A new channel was going to launch and many people were making pilots, agreements were already signed. I also made a programme ‘Life Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega’,” he shared in an interview with Siddharth Kannan.The actor-director said he had invested the money from the sale of his house into the project, only to discover that the channel had vanished.“Suddenly, I got to know that the channel has disappeared. I had invested the money that I got from selling the flat in that programme. I thought that I had a first-class life, a 4-BHK house, everything set for the family. And then, the channel disappeared and no one knew what happened.. there was just a lock on their door.”With no work coming in and the pressure of paying rent mounting, Raju turned to Anupam, believing his elder brother would help him financially. However, Anupam was himself going through a difficult phase professionally.“I also felt the pressure to pay the rent. I had no one else, I could only talk to my brother, and I thought he will help me. But at that time, he had also stopped working. The reason was that he didn’t want to do any of those weird films, he wanted substantial roles. So, I felt that my brother did not help me out. ‘He could have done so,’ that was my thought at that time.”Raju said his understanding of Anupam's situation changed after he happened to read an interview in a magazine. A particular statement about his personal life made him realise that he had been assuming that his brother had no problems simply because he was financially successful.“Then, I was reading a magazine on the toilet. In the interview, Anupam Kher had said, ‘I wish I had my own child’. Although, he considers Sikander his own child. But then I never thought about my brother in that light. We took him for granted, thinking he doesn’t have any problems because he was doing well financially. We never thought that what was going on in his life.”The realisation changed the way Raju looked at expectations and relationships. He said the year 2000 became a turning point in his life and taught him to understand what others could be going through before expecting anything from them.“That was the thing that changed the whole concept of my life. Have expectations but don’t do it like that. Try to find out what is going in the other person’s life as well. I am talking about the year 2000, the year that changed my whole life, my thinking. On that day, I stopped expecting anything from anyone, no matter who it is.”Raju also recalled how he eventually found his way back to work after months of financial and professional uncertainty. He said he had even tried suggestions involving rings, rituals and prayers before deciding to leave everything to fate.“When your time is bad, your expenses tend to increase. Some suggested wearing certain rings, doing rituals, prayers, I got those done too. Work had also stopped coming. After a few months, I told my wife that we should trust in God, let’s see what happens, and I removed all the rings. The next day, I got a call for work. I got an offer for a TV serial. I instantly agreed and told them to pay whatever they want. Life started again,” he concluded.Interestingly, earlier this year, Anupam Kher had spoken about his bond with Raju during an interaction with Zindagi with Richa YouTube channel. He revealed that he has been financially supporting his younger brother for years and said that he has never kept track of how much money he has given him.“If every brother remembers what they were like when they were young, there would be no fight. I look at my life like it’s a film. How can I forget that we grew up together? I must also compliment Kirron (Kher, wife), because she never, ever asked me, ‘Why do you do so much for your brother?’ That’s how problems begin. I would sign cheques for Raju, the household, and other things… I told my manager long ago, ‘Remember one thing in life, never ask me how much money I’m giving to my brother’.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Fire breaks out on Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi's 'Ramayana' temporary set; no injuries reported
articles.summary: A fire broke out at a temporary set in Mumbai’s Film City on Monday, October 5, 2026. The set was of Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi’s 'Ramayana'.
articles.body: A fire broke out at a temporary set in Mumbai’s Film City on Monday, October 5, 2026. The set was of Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi’s 'Ramayana'. Thick smoke was seen rising from the area, and videos of the fire went viral on social media. The fire brigade confirmed that no one was injured in the incident.What happened on the 'Ramayana' setAccording to the Mid-Day report, flames and thick smoke were seen at the location, which caused worry among people on social media. Sharing an update, a netizen tweeted, "A fire reportedly broke out on Nitesh Tiwari's much-awaited Ramayana set, sending a huge plume of smoke into the air and triggering panic at the location."What the Mumbai Fire Brigade saidAccording to the BMC's Mumbai Fire Brigade, a Level-I fire was reported at 4.02 pm behind Reliance Media Works and Prime Focus in Film City, Goregaon East. The blaze was limited to electric wiring, cables and fittings, along with doors, wooden planks, AC units, bamboo, plastic items, sound systems and shooting equipment. All of this was inside a PCR unit on a 100x20-foot temporary set behind Prime Focus Studio.The fire was put out by 4.55 pm. The fire brigade, police, BMC ward control and 108 ambulance services reached the spot. No injuries were reported.Other shoots are also affectedThe shoots of MTV's 'Hustle 5' and 'Pati Patni Aur Panga 2' were also disturbed, as both are being filmed in nearby studios. Early reports suggest the fire began on the 'Pati Patni Aur Panga 2' set and then moved towards the 'Hustle 5' set. There is no official word yet on how badly either set has been damaged.About 'Ramayana'The incident comes soon after YouTuber MrBeast attended a 'Ramayana' event in Mumbai with Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Ravie Dubey, Namit Malhotra and Nitesh Tiwari. articles.title: In 2009, Keanu Reeves opened up about his private foundation supporting cancer research; here’s the truth behind his reported 70% Matrix donation
articles.summary: Keanu Reeves has often kept his charitable work away from the spotlight.
articles.body: Keanu Reeves has often kept his charitable work away from the spotlight. The Matrix star has supported cancer-related causes for years, a cause that has a deeply personal connection for him following his sister Kim Reeves’ battle with leukemia.However, a widely circulated claim that Reeves donated 70% of his earnings from The Matrix to cancer research is not accurate. According to a 2022 report by The Independent, Reeves’ publicist directly denied the claim, telling Newsweek that the actor “did not donate 70 per cent of his salary to charity.”The viral $31.5 million claimThe claim suggested that Reeves earned around $45 million from The Matrix and subsequently donated 70% of it, approximately $31.5 million to cancer research following his sister’s illness.The figure was widely circulated online and picked up by several publications, particularly around the release of The Matrix Resurrections. But the calculation was based on a claim that was never reliably established. With Reeves’ publicist denying the donation story, the $31.5 million figure should not be treated as a confirmed charitable contribution.Interestingly, the story appeared believable partly because Reeves genuinely has a history of supporting cancer-related causes.Keanu Reeves stood by sister Kim during her leukemia battleReeves’ sister Kim was diagnosed with leukemia in the 1990s. The actor was reportedly closely involved in supporting her during her long battle with the disease.In a 1999 interview, Kim spoke about the support she received from her brother during her illness. Her comments were later reported by The Independent, which noted that Reeves would stay by her side and comfort her when her pain became severe.Kim eventually went into remission, but her experience remained an important part of Reeves’ connection with cancer-related causes.Reeves confirmed his private foundation in 2009One of the most firmly documented parts of the story comes directly from Reeves himself.As reported by Ladies Home Journal, the actor revealed that he had been running a private foundation for around five or six years. He said that the foundation helped support children’s hospitals and cancer research.Reeves also explained why the organisation was not publicly associated with him. He said, “I don’t like to attach my name to it,” adding that he preferred to let the foundation do what it does. His comments were reported by The Independent and have also been cited by The Dad in its coverage of the actor’s philanthropy.This means that while the exact amount of money Reeves contributed through the foundation has not been publicly established, his own 2009 comments confirm that he was privately supporting children’s hospitals and cancer research.His cancer-related support continuedReeves’ involvement with cancer-related causes has continued over the years. He participated in a Stand Up to Cancer telethon in 2008 and later used his celebrity to raise money for Camp Rainbow Gold, a charity supporting children affected by cancer.In 2020, he auctioned a 15-minute virtual date with himself to raise funds for the organisation. The fundraiser attracted significant attention and bidding. These documented examples are separate from the disputed $31.5 million donation claim and offer a clearer picture of Reeves’ charitable involvement.The real story behind the viral claimThe most accurate version of the story is therefore slightly different from what has circulated online.There is no reliable evidence that Keanu Reeves donated 70% of his $45 million Matrix earnings, and his publicist specifically denied that claim. What is established is that his sister Kim battled leukemia, Reeves supported her during her illness, and he later confirmed that he had a private foundation supporting children’s hospitals and cancer research.His decision to keep that foundation private is perhaps the most telling part of the story. In an industry where celebrity philanthropy is often publicised, Reeves told Ladies Home Journal in 2009 that he did not want his name attached to the foundation and preferred to let its work speak for itself.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Olivia Dean’s ‘I’ve Seen It’ copied melody of Bill Withers classic ‘Just the Two of Us,’ lawsuit alleges
articles.summary: Olivia Dean is accused of copying the melody of Bill Withers’ Grammy-winning hit song “Just the Two of Us” for the closing track of her latest album.
articles.body: Olivia Dean is accused of copying the melody of Bill Withers’ Grammy-winning hit song “Just the Two of Us” for the closing track of her latest album. A lawsuit was filed Thursday in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, alleging that Dean’s “I’ve Seen It” copies “in large and significant part” Withers’ song. Mattie Music Group, which controls Withers’ catalog, says in the suit that it used a musicologist who compared the two songs and found “substantial similarities.” The defendants — Capitol Records, Universal Music Group, Sony Publishing, and Kobalt Music Publishing America — were notified in writing in August of the infringement, the lawsuit says. None of the defendants immediately responded to a request for comment on Monday. NBC News reached out to the Withers estate and Dean for comment. Dean is not named as a defendant in the lawsuit. “Despite receiving notice, defendants continued reproducing, distributing, licensing, publicly performing, and commercially exploiting the infringing work,” the suit states. “Just the Two of Us” was performed by jazz saxophonist Grover Washington Jr. with lead vocals by Withers, who died in 2020. It was released to radio stations in 1981, becoming a huge hit for Withers. The song reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart and won a Grammy for Best R&B Song, according to the lawsuit. Mattie Music Group says in the lawsuit that because of the song’s success and “decades of radio play,” the defendants had a reasonable opportunity to hear the song before creating “I’ve Seen It.” “I’ve Seen It” is featured on Dean’s album “The Art of Loving,” which won her Best New Artist at the Grammy Awards in February.

articles.title: 21-day Vijayadashami fest begins with traditional rituals in Buxar
articles.summary: Buxar’s historic 21-day Vijayadashami Ram Leela began at Kila Maidan with Vedic rituals, Ganesh Puja and Narad Moh Leela by Vrindavan artists.
articles.body: Buxar: Buxar’s historic 21-day Vijayadashami festival began with religious fervour at Kila Maidan on Sunday evening, with Vedic chants, Ganesh Puja and traditional rituals marking the opening of the celebrations.The festival, a pre-Independence tradition spanning more than a century, is being organised with a mix of religious and cultural programmes. A large number of devotees and spectators gathered at Kila Maidan for the inaugural ceremony and the subsequent staging of ‘Narad Moh Leela’ by artists from Vrindavan.The festival was inaugurated by Mahant Rajgopalacharya ‘Tyagi Ji’ Maharaj, Peethadhishwar of Lakshmi Narayan Temple, who performed the rituals and offered blessings. Education minister Mithilesh Tiwari also attended the programme.The Ramleela complex reverberated with Vedic chants as scholars performed the traditional rituals. The inaugural ceremony was followed by worship of Lord Ganesha and Lord Ram and Janaki, ‘aarti’ and the staging of ‘Narad Moh Leela’.The performance, directed by Swami Mohan Shyam Bhardwaj, depicted the story of Devarshi Narad, his penance, the emergence of ego from his devotion and his eventual self-realisation through Lord Vishnu’s divine Leela.Buxar’s Ramleela is distinctive for its 21-day format. The celebrations begin around Jitiya festival and continue until the traditional Bharat Milap following Dussehra. The festival culminates with Bharat Milap at Yamuna Chowk.This year, the Balkrishna Raslila Ramleela Mandal of Vrindavan is staging Ramleela and Krishnaleela. Krishnaleela will be performed daily from 9 am to noon, while Ramleela will be staged from 8 pm to 10 pm.During the inaugural programme, many women observed religious fasts.The education minister said Buxar’s Ramleela was a cultural tradition dating back to the pre-Independence era and had a unique identity in Bihar.He said the performances conveyed the ideals of Lord Ram, including ‘maryada’, sacrifice, truth and dharma, and stressed the need to preserve the tradition for future generations.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: CNN’s boss will remain as Paramount and WBD merge into Skydance
articles.summary: ﻿The entertainment giant has outlined its new leadership.
articles.body: CNN CEO Mark Thompson will remain at the head of the news network when Paramount’s $110 billion Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition closes this week. Thompson wrote in a memo to employees that he believes the combined company will “fully support the principle and practice of the kind of independent news that CNN has always stood for,” according to a report from The New York Times. The news comes as part of an announcement detailing the combined company’s executive leadership. Paramount CEO David Ellison will lead the companies — to be called Skydance — alongside former Mattel head Ynon Kreiz. Speculation about what would become of CNN swirled following the news of the media megamerger, which puts WBD’s CNN and Paramount’s CBS News under the same roof. As part of a settlement reached with 12 states, Skydance must adopt a news editorial independence board. The entertainment giant revealed the rest of its executive lineup as well, with HBO CEO Casey Bloys serving as the chief content officer of Skydance’s streaming business. Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg will head up Skydance’s film studios, while George Cheeks will run its TV business. Bari Weiss, who was appointed editor-in-chief of CBS News last year, will remain in her role even as ratings decline. Paramount’s acquisition is expected to close on Tuesday.
